headline: Seasonal Coastal Access and Day-Use Policies
reservation: Taylor Head is a day-use park; no overnight camping is permitted within the park boundaries. While entry permits are not currently required for day use, the park is seasonal, typically operating from mid-May to October; check official Nova Scotia Provincial Parks alerts for gate closures.

days.title: Granite Barrens and Sand Beaches

stops.name: Psyche Cove Beach
stops.detail: Walk the white sands of this secluded cove, known for its turquoise waters and granite outcrops.

stops.name: Headland Trail
stops.detail: Hike the rugged loop through the coastal barrens to see the exposed geological features of the Eastern Shore.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour 45 minutes from Halifax via Highway 7; conditions vary.
days.note: The coastal weather can change rapidly; fog is common even when the interior is sunny.

days.title: Eastern Shore Coastal Exploration

stops.name: Spry Bay
stops.detail: Observe the unique drumlin islands from the shoreline lookoffs before entering the park.

stops.name: Bob Bluff Trail
stops.detail: Take this shorter path for a high-angle view of the rugged coastline and offshore islands.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes from Sheet Harbour; road conditions are generally stable.
days.note: Black flies and mosquitoes can be prevalent in the wooded sections during June and July.

days.title: Tidal Pools and Marine Life

stops.name: Bull Beach
stops.detail: Explore the rocky intertidal zones to find local marine life during low tide.

stops.name: Taylor Head Interpretive Panels
stops.detail: Read about the cultural history of the former settlement and the unique flora of the barrens.

days.driving: Internal park roads are short; allow 10 minutes between trailheads.
days.note: Check local tide tables before visiting Bull Beach to safely explore the rocky flats.

intel.title: Beach Access Lots
intel.text: The main lot near Psyche Cove can fill on warm summer weekends. Arrive before noon to secure a spot close to the primary trailhead and beach facilities.

intel.title: Eastern Shore Connectivity
intel.text: Cell service is intermittent along Highway 7 and often drops within the park's forested trails. Plan your route and download maps before leaving Sheet Harbour.

intel.title: Sheet Harbour Services
intel.text: Sheet Harbour is the nearest hub for fuel, ice, and groceries. There are no retail services or potable water stations within the park itself.

intel.title: Seasonal Gate Closures
intel.text: The park gate is typically locked outside of the summer season (November to May). During this time, the park is accessible only by foot from the highway entrance.

intel.title: Facility Availability
intel.text: Pit toilets are available seasonally at the trailheads. There are no indoor facilities or equipment rentals available within this wilderness-oriented park.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Halifax Stanfield (YHZ), take Highway 102 to 107, then merge onto the Marine Drive (Highway 7).
plan.vehicle: A standard vehicle is suitable for the paved and gravel access roads; avoid parking on soft shoulders.
plan.goldenHour: The Headland Trail offers 360-degree views of the Atlantic, ideal for viewing the sunrise over the eastern horizon.
